newsitem.title: GERMANY: Building union, employers make progress in talks.
newsitem.headline: Building union, employers make progress in talks.

text.p: German construction union IG Bau and employers continued their wage talks on Friday morning after making progress on the key issue of sick pay during negotiations which were adjourned last night, employers said.
The two sides have called a news conference for 0800 GMT on Friday to provide details on the current state of talks.

Neither the IG Bau union nor negotiators from the construction employers' side would say whether an agreement had been reached which could avert the threat of the first large scale strike in the troubled industry since 1950.
But asked whether the talks were now likely to make fast progress, IB Bau chairman Klaus Wiesenhuegel said: "I think so."
Time is running out before a May 21 deadline when a strike ballot could be called.
Talks resumed after the union's wages commission on Monday rejected a proposed deal reached in arbitration talks last week.
That deal offered a 1.3 percent pay rise from April 1 -- below the rate of German inflation -- a 20 percent cut in sick pay for the first three weeks of illness, and a cut in Christmas bonus.
The sick pay cut was the main bone of contention.
The union also said it would not consider any new pay deal brokered by the arbitrator, the Christian Democrat politician Heiner Geissler, and that Geissler could attend the talks only as a moderator.
Wiesenhuegel has said the union is prepared to compensate for full payment of sick-pay benefits but said it was "a matter of principle" to defend the rights of workers to sick pay.
